correctness.rationale: For independent stages the mean-square factor is F(z)^N. Exact gain identity (1) is verified. The two-point imaginary-axis numerator is affine in y²; its highest coefficient B changes sign exactly at p_*(a,b). For p≤p_* both imaginary-axis boundary and the high-frequency limit are bounded by one, while subharmonic maximum principle and strict interior small-step contraction give F<1 over the open left half-plane. For p>p_* an imaginary-axis instability persists inside by continuity. A strict monotone covariance identity proves failure of centered nonconstant laws; analytic expansion and implicit-function theorem yield kappa y⁴/2. A standalone stdlib verifier passes 396 rational assertions and does not purport to prove infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary full text treats the law Uniform[0,1] and proves failure of mean-square A-stability for that fixed law. The new exact two-atom probability cutoff, including its stable endpoint, does not follow from that uniform-specific conclusion; a universal obstruction for every nonconstant centered law and its distribution-dependent fourth-order coefficient are additionally proved. The earlier accessible local record 933cbee0-4d10-4d06-8c4d-3a655827d88b covers the uniform-law global boundary only and is not claimed as new. The source laws and implications were compared, not titles alone. Specialist publication precedence remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated analysis of random two-atom theta coefficients or equivalent resolvent mixtures could already contain the phase boundary.
The classic stochastic theta-method SDE paper was examined at the abstract/model level, not full text; its model has multiplicative SDE noise and fixed theta.
A semantic database search returning no matching result does not prove originality.

value.rationale: The exact two-atom threshold is a complete nontrivial design classification for random implicitness in a canonical stiffness test: it separates distributions that retain full mean-square A-stability from those that do not and includes the sharp borderline. It shows the stability cost of preserving the midpoint mean and quantifies the fourth-order weak-damping notch for any centered law. The result is materially more informative than the known uniform-only failure and has clear limits to scalar iid test equations.
